subject: Post-call recap: Acme TCO discussion and next steps
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <carlos.vega@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Feb 2027 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme TCO discussion and next steps

Hi Carlos / Lena —

Thanks for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed so we're all aligned. If I've missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain & goals
- Latency-sensitive customer-facing assistants: target p95 < 400ms across the cluster.
- Current spend: ~ $45k/month across existing endpoints; wanting to avoid 3x cost growth as usage ramps.
- Top priorities: predictable cost, consistent latency, and data isolation for PI/finance flows.

Estimated token economics (back-of-envelope)
- Expected monthly usage from your pilot: ~15M total tokens (2.5M input, 12.5M output).
- Current hosted per-token baseline we discussed: $0.0004 per token equivalent -> ~ $6,000/month.
- With dedicated capacity + batching/caching profile, we estimate a 20-40% reduction in unit cost for steady-state traffic.

Key levers we recommend
1) Prefix / KV caching for repeated prompts: likely to reduce generated tokens by ~25-35% for your bot flows (FAQ + templated answers).
2) Aggressive batching on non-real-time routes: combine short async inference requests into 32-64 request batches during business hours.
3) Quantization profile for your medium-length responses: same quality with ~2-3x throughput improvement on T4/A10x hardware.
4) Model routing: use a cheaper compatible model for non-critical routes (metrics capture to validate quality).

Draft ROI framing (pilot -> production)
- Pilot baseline (hosted): ~$6k/mo.
- Expected production with Redwood Dedicated + caching/batching: ~$3.6k-$4.8k/mo (20-40% savings on unit + bulk throughput benefit).
- Additional one-time implementation ramp (batching/caching tuning, QA): estimate 2-3 engineer-weeks.

Next steps we agreed
- I'll share a downloadable TCO workbook with the detailed line items (attached).
- Your team to share: current average prompt length and 1-2 representative prompt sets (to validate caching opportunities).
- Follow-up: technical deep-dive with Rafael and Marissa next Tuesday, 10:00 AM PT. Rafael to send calendar invite.

Attachments
- acme-tco-breakdown-20270205.xlsx (spreadsheet) includes token assumptions, per-model cost scenarios, and sensitivity analysis.

Thanks again, looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0182

--

Thanks Avery, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from our side:

- The current $45k/mo number includes model training infra and unrelated ML workloads; for the bot pilot we expect the LLM inference portion to be closer to $7k-$9k/month on our current stack (so your baseline estimate is helpful).
- Latency SLO: for the web assistant 400ms p95 is correct; mobile-target p95 is 250-200ms.
- On caching: ~60% of our user sessions hit identical or near-identical prompts because of templated flows; we're optimistic caching gains could be higher than 25%.

I'll upload two prompt sets and the usage histogram to the shared folder by EOD. Also, if you can include a quick model-comparison appendix in the workbook (latency vs. cost for the two models we discussed), that'd be useful for our infra team.

Appreciate the clear next steps.
